name: AI GridWatch data center project tracker
caveat:
A working set of identified proposals a community can track, not a census — most of the country's activity is not in here yet. Pennsylvania is the exception: its rows are synced from PA DEP's own data-center permit tracker, so the state's coverage is close to complete and carries the permit trail with it.

**Each row carries its own provenance.** Rows showing a verification date link to reporting or the governing body's own record and were read on that date; rows marked *unverified* have no source on record — a lead to check, not a fact to cite.

**Stage is derived, not asserted.** *Hearing scheduled*, *Awaiting decision*, *Approved* and *Withdrawn* are computed from each row's milestone dates on every rebuild, so a hearing date that has passed stops reading 'scheduled'. Hearings get moved and projects re-file under new names — treat a scheduled date as the earliest to act by, and confirm with the clerk before relying on it. Leads are mined into data/project_candidates.json and promoted here only after a human reads a primary source.

schema.name: Project or code name.
schema.filing_llc: Shell LLC on the filing (ties to the campus registry), or blank.
schema.locality: Town or county the project sits in.
schema.size_mw: Planned IT/critical load in MW, or blank.
schema.announced: ISO date first publicly proposed, or blank.
schema.rezoning_filed: ISO date the rezoning/permit application was filed, or blank.
schema.hearing_date: ISO date of the next/decisive public hearing, or blank.
schema.decided_date: ISO date a terminal decision was reached, or blank.
schema.outcome: approved | denied | withdrawn | blank (blank = still live).
schema.stage: DERIVED status shown on the page (Hearing scheduled, Awaiting decision, In review, Proposed, Rumored, Approved, Under construction, Operating, Denied, Withdrawn, Blocked by ban).
schema.days_to_hearing: DERIVED days until the hearing (negative once past), or blank.
schema.source: Primary URL backing the current status.
schema.as_of: ISO date the source was read, or blank.
schema.verified: true if a source is on record.

projects.name: Dickerson Data Center Campus (Atmosphere)
projects.note: Atmosphere Data Centers (which took over the project from Terra Innovations, whose initial conditional-use application dates to January 2024) proposes a five-building data center campus on 110 acres at the decommissioned Dickerson Generating Station coal plant site; a major modification to the conditional use was filed in December 2025 and amended plans are on Montgomery Planning's development database. On 2026-07-28 the Montgomery County Council approved an 18-month moratorium on new data center approvals that encompasses this proposal; Office of Zoning and Administrative Appeals hearings had been scheduled for Sept 10-11, 2026.

events.summary: As reported December 4, 2025, the county hearing examiner had granted Terra Energy conditional use approval (case CU 24-13) for a data center complex at the Dickerson site, with the number and square footage of buildings left to future modifications.
Office of Zoning and Administrative Appeals hearings on the conditional-use modification scheduled for Sept 10-11, 2026.

The Office of Zoning and Administrative Hearings lists the hearing on case CU 24-13(a)(A) (Atmosphere Dickerson Property Owner, LLC; conditional use holder Terra Energy, LLC) as scheduled for Thursday and Friday, November 12 and 13, 2026, at 9:30 a.m.

projects.name: 900 Conshohocken Road data center (former Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill)
projects.note: 900 Conshohocken Road LLC seeks a special exception from Plymouth Township's zoning hearing board to convert the recently closed Cleveland-Cliffs steel mill — 10 existing buildings totaling about 2 million sq ft on 66 acres along the Schuylkill River — into a data center. The Aug. 6 hearing nearly filled a 750-seat auditorium; Conshohocken Borough was granted party status while Norristown was denied. The board set a procedural-only session for Aug. 17, with testimony continuing in September; an opposition petition has topped 4,000 signatures.

events.summary: The Plymouth Township Planning Agency voted 4-0 not to recommend a special exception to allow a data center at 900 Conshohocken Road.

The zoning hearing kicked off at Colonial Middle School focused on procedural matters; party status was granted to Plymouth Township, the property owner's representatives, nearby residents, and the Borough of Conshohocken Authority, with no testimony taken.

Zoning hearing board session at Colonial Middle School drew a nearly full 750-seat auditorium; the applicant's engineer began testimony comparing the data center to permitted heavy-industrial uses, and party-status requests from neighboring municipalities and residents were taken up.

At the Zoning Hearing Board session, residents booed and cursed as a witness testified data centers resemble manufacturing; the board rejected several legal motions filed by opponents and indicated it would continue the case in September.
Hearing continued to Aug. 17 for procedural matters only, with no witness testimony; further testimony to be scheduled.

projects.name: EdgeCore Shannon Hill campus
projects.note: 697 acres purchased in the Shannon Hill Regional Business Park for a 3.9M sq ft, 1.1+ GW campus - a $17B+ investment announced June 2025, phased over several years. No construction start date or tenants disclosed at announcement. Part of a data-center surge in a small county that already hosts an AWS campus.

events.summary: Louisa County Board of Supervisors voted 6-1 to authorize a $2,620,000 budget supplement (Resolution RES-2019-40) for the purchase of approximately 700 acres in the Shannon Hill area for a regional business park, having previously voted to exercise purchase options on January 22, 2019.
EdgeCore announced the land purchase (697 ac, Shannon Hill Regional Business Park) and $17B+ phased campus plan in June 2025; construction timing and tenants undisclosed.

EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure announced the purchase of 697 acres at Shannon Hill Regional Business Park for $42 million and plans for a 1.1+ GW, 3.9 million sq ft data center campus with $17 billion total investment.

projects.name: King of Prussia campus (MLP Ventures)
projects.note: Five-site, 4.6M sq ft campus; Board of Supervisors denied extension requests and preliminary land development proposals Aug 14, 2026. Developer filed lawsuit; judge vacated injunction, finding township review fair. 20,000-signature petition against. Developer plans to appeal.

events.summary: Applications filed in early March 2026, ~10 days before Upper Merion's new data-center ordinance took effect - grandfathering the projects out of its residential buffer, noise, and water-use requirements.
The 4.6M sq ft, five-site plan by MLP Ventures was publicly unveiled; neighbor pushback began immediately.
In July 2026 the Upper Merion Planning Commission voted against three of the data-center proposals; hundreds of residents packed hearings in opposition. Township review continues.

Board of Supervisors denied extension requests and preliminary land development proposals. Developer had filed lawsuit seeking extension but judge vacated injunction, finding township review fair. 20,000-signature petition against the project.
Board of Supervisors denied. 20,000-signature petition. Developer lawsuit dismissed by judge.

projects.name: Microsoft Person County
projects.note: Multi-billion dollar data center campus on 1,350 acres in Person County, North Carolina.

events.summary: Person County announced Microsoft had purchased roughly 1,350 acres in Woodsdale Township for approximately $26.85 million, forming the Person County Mega Park site; the buyer identity and intended use were not disclosed at the time.
Economic development director completed the rezoning application covering the Microsoft parcels; the abstract named the parcels but did not name the client or intended use.
Person County commissioners voted to approve the rezoning for the Microsoft data center parcels, passing with little friction under generic bureaucratic language.

projects.name: PORTS Technology Campus (SoftBank)
projects.note: Leased land on DOE's former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant site. Billed as potentially world's largest AI data center at 10GW full buildout (phase 1 is 800MW), paired with 9.2GW on-site gas plant ($33.3B) and $4.2B in new AEP Ohio transmission.

events.summary: DOE, SoftBank/SB Energy, and AEP Ohio formally announced a partnership to develop the PORTS Technology Campus, pairing a 10GW data center with up to 9.2GW of new natural gas generation on the Portsmouth site.

Federal officials and SoftBank's chairman held a groundbreaking ceremony for the PORTS Technology Campus, a 10GW data center project billed as potentially the world's largest, part of a $500B investment tied to the U.S.-Japan Strategic Trade and Investment Agreement, including $33.3B in Japanese-backed funding for the natural gas generation component.

projects.name: Microsoft Three Mile Island (Crane Clean Energy Center)
projects.note: $1.6B power purchase agreement to restart TMI Unit 1 (renamed Crane Clean Energy Center) by 2028; Microsoft will buy 100% of the 835MW nuclear output for 20 years to power its AI data centers.

events.summary: Constellation Energy announced a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to restart the 835 MW Three Mile Island Unit 1, renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center, to supply carbon-free power for Microsoft data centers; the deal is expected to create ~3,400 jobs and add $16 billion to Pennsylvania GDP.

projects.name: Midtown Data Center
projects.note: 120 MW / $3B campus near the Armory; CUP upheld with conditions (no diesel testing on bad air days, on-site renewables) after 11-hour hearing.

events.summary: Board of Adjustment unanimously upheld CUP with air-quality and renewables conditions.

projects.name: Deep Green downtown data center
projects.note: 24 MW data center plus a 16 MW fuel-cell plant on 2.5 acres near the Grand River downtown, with a closed-loop water-glycol cooling system (~500,000 gal/yr). The Planning Commission recommended the rezoning 5-2 in March 2026, but Deep Green withdrew its rezoning request on April 6, 2026, ending the proposal before a council vote.

events.summary: Lansing City Planning Commission voted 5-2 to recommend the rezoning for the 24 MW data center + 16 MW fuel-cell plant.
Deep Green withdrew its rezoning application, axing the downtown proposal before City Council voted.

projects.name: Project Riverjump (Marion)
projects.note: Code-named hyperscale data center proposed for the west side of the City of Marion, the county seat. Because Marion is incorporated, the county's 24-month moratorium (Ordinance 4-2026) never applied to it. Rumors of a data center west of Marion near Central Indiana Ethanol circulated from January 2026; the mayor said then that no ordinance or vote was scheduled. In late August 2026, citing public feedback in person and online, the mayor said he would not pursue or support data center development in Marion under his administration. The developer and end user were never publicly identified; no application appears in the public record.

events.summary: Chronicle-Tribune reported the City of Marion is no longer moving forward with Project Riverjump, a hyperscale data center planned for the city's west side; the mayor said that based on citizen feedback he 'will not be pursuing or supporting data center development in the City of Marion under my administration.'

projects.name: Project Taurus (Raeden)
projects.note: Retrofit of an existing building on Garden of the Gods Road into the city's first AI data center, by California-based Raeden. Administratively approved by city staff in June 2026; the planning commission denied residents' appeals after a marathon hearing; two new appeals now send it to City Council, whose hearing must fall between Aug 29 and Sept 28 (likely mid-September - date not yet set). Chelsea Glen neighbors cite power, water, and noise from a prior Bitcoin operation at the site.

events.summary: KKTV reported that Oakland, California-based Raeden proposed 'Project Taurus,' a roughly 50-megawatt data center to replace a former Intel manufacturing plant near Garden of the Gods, and that a neighborhood meeting to hear resident concerns was scheduled for April 7, 2026, at the Hyatt Place hotel.
City planning department administratively approved the Project Taurus application in June 2026; neighbors immediately announced an appeal.

KRDO reported the city Planning Department administratively approved the Development Plan Modification on June 11, 2026, for the 21.96-acre former Intel site at 1565 High Tech Way, with residents given until 5 p.m. on June 22 to file appeals.
Planning Commission denied the citizens' appeals after a ~14-hour hearing, upholding the approval 6-2.

projects.name: Karis Critical Plum Farms Data Center
projects.note: Karis Critical acquired 180 acres known as Plum Farms at the northwest corner of Route 59 and Higgins Road for $45 million and sought rezoning for a data center. The village planning commission gave a negative recommendation in early June 2026. After weeks of community backlash, Karis notified the village on July 1 that it would withdraw the rezoning request. The governor had also suspended state data center incentives. Karis has not indicated whether it will refile.

events.summary: Karis Critical withdraws rezoning request after community opposition.

projects.name: DC Blox Warren Township (Thunderbird Commerce Center)
projects.note: Up to $2.2B (incl. IT equipment) campus at 305 Fintail Drive in the Thunderbird Commerce Center (former Ford Visteon plant site), near S. Kitley Ave. and the Pennsy Trail. Originally 3 buildings; scaled back on July 8, 2026 to 2 buildings, 25 fewer backup diesel generators, and 28 MW less power demand after community pushback. Exempted from Indianapolis's Aug. 19, 2026 citywide data-center moratorium as a previously-approved project. DC Blox says the project creates 35 permanent high-wage jobs.

events.summary: The MDC hearing examiner held a hearing on the DC Blox petition; residents said they felt they lacked a voice in the decision-making process.
The Metropolitan Development Commission voted 6-1 to approve the scaled-back DC Blox data-center campus despite dozens of protesters outside the City-County Building.

projects.name: Antelope Data Campus (Project Antelope)
projects.note: Iron County Planning Commission unanimously approved a conditional use permit on 2026-06-04 for Pronghorn Development LLC's five-building campus (up to 6.75M sq ft, with an on-site natural gas plant of up to 1.5 GW) on 640 acres along Antelope Springs Road, about 8 miles west of Cedar City, with 62 conditions covering water rights, wastewater, noise, lighting and site restoration. The application was vested before a county moratorium on new data center applications adopted the month prior; additional permits are still required before construction. Buildout is proposed in phases over 8-10 years.

events.summary: Pronghorn Development LLC submitted a conditional use permit application in November 2025 for the 640-acre Antelope Data Campus, months after the county amended its zoning ordinance to allow data centers.

Iron County Planning Commission unanimously approved a conditional use permit for the Antelope Data Campus with 62 conditions; the application was vested under existing ordinance ahead of the county's data center moratorium.

projects.name: Project Iron Spur
projects.note: ~129-acre hyperscale campus proposed across from Rural Hall town hall; Forsyth County Planning Board recommended denial. Commissioners held the public hearing July 30, 2026 - decision pending.

events.summary: Charlotte-based developer Drox Group LLC presented its proposed hyperscale data center on roughly 129 acres in Rural Hall at a March community meeting, where residents raised concerns about noise, pollution, and energy and water demands.
County commissioners held the public hearing on the rezoning after months of resident opposition; a final decision was pending as of this record.
The Forsyth County Board of Commissioners voted 5-2 to deny the rezoning request for Project Iron Spur, following six months of review, over 400 emails, and dozens of public speakers.
